title: Viewport: orthographic (parallel) projection option
body:
## What are you trying to do

I machine plates and brackets on my LinuxCNC machine, and most of my viewport time is setup work: looking straight at a side to line something up, judging an edge for parallelism, checking the part against the world axes, and reading the toolpath overlays. The view cube gives me the orientation (top/front/side is one click), but the projection stays perspective: edges converge, the silhouette drifts while I orbit or zoom, and a side view never looks "straight" the way a machinist's square looks straight. For CAM layout work I want a parallel (orthographic) projection most of the time.

This is the normal CAD/CAM convention - Fusion 360 defaults to a parallel projection with a perspective toggle next to it, and OnShape and SolidWorks do the same.

## How you imagine it working

- A Perspective / Orthographic radio pair beside the Shaded/Wireframe radios in the viewport panel. Default stays Perspective, so the current look never changes on open.
- A keyboard shortcut for the flip, in the same layer as the existing F/V/... keys.
- In ortho mode, the wheel scales the view height instead of the orbit distance; zoom-to-cursor stays cursor-anchored; and picking and every overlay (toolpaths, boundary viz, the view-cube HUD) read the same matrix the draw does, so nothing drifts.
- The view-cube face views become true ortho views in that mode. The mode rides as view state - a direct field flip like the display mode, never a command, never saved into the project.

Happy to build this - claim comment to follow.
